title: Step by Step or let Claude fully plan?
author: Vaveidan
selftext:
Hey,  
I want to create my own 3D MMORPG with Three.js with Claude Code. Now my question is should I tell fable "Create the WHOLE Game Development Plan + Roadmap for me" or should I tell him step by step. "I want to make my own MMO, lets start by coding the Player Model + Animations", "Now lets create the Terrain". etc. (If u understand what I mean).

Because If I let Claude create a full game via Roadmap & Docs it always tends to look messy and "base three.js".

Thanks fo ur help!

comments.author: Exhales_Deeply
comments.body:
i think you’re already hitting a brick wall when you say your “own” MMORPG

but that aside, if you’re looking for a specific aesthetic and style, start by defining that

replies.author: Vaveidan
replies.body: With my test project it works pretty good so far. Let's just say "Multiplayer Game" as it is a RPG for my friends and me to play around with. Network works, Anti-Cheat works baseline etc. Just the Design is not what I want yet. Maybe I should just link Assets for ThreeJS to claude and tell him "use that".

replies.author: SillyYou8433
replies.body:
I think you either are misunderstanding what an MMORPG is, or you're underestimating the scale of hosting one.

An MMORPG requires a dedicated server to run constantly AND support the scale of players that comes with the word "massive" in that title. Peer to peer, which is likely what you did with your friends is much easier to set up

replies.author: ActuallyAdasi
replies.body:
My guess is OP wants client-server architecture, and a persistent game world. Something that *could* scale, but doesn’t have to because it’s just him and his buddies.

I’d suggest going as iteratively as possible, there’s no value other than Reddit clout for saying you “one shotted” the prompt, and there is likely significant cost in terms of quality of the product or alignment with your direction.

comments.author: KHRZ
comments.body: No matter what you choose, you'll likely do many sessions. I've done 10,000 sessions so far for my game, most of them are asking the agent to fix the same bug 3-4 times. So your 1st prompt is likely a very tiny investment in comparison, so I would just experiment and see how that goes. Most important part is not to let the AI think all your existing code is some VIP code that must be kept intact at all costs, because otherwise it will waste tons of time making unit tests to preserve what it generated earliers on a whim. I would tell it to just throw away and remake stuff in the beginning phase, make sure you can make big moves for as long as possible before things slow down.

replies.author: Vaveidan
replies.body: I'm deep down too already. Almost 450 Commits deep so far. Stay strong soldier✅

replies.author: Ray_Light91
replies.body: Have the AI write the correct tests to prevent regressions! My codebase for tests is nearly the same size as the codebase for the game itself! 7 months in and source code is 134.5k LoC over 1000+ files (android game)

comments.author: vexmach1ne
comments.body:
I like to start vibecoding online games with a solid working LAN netcode foundation. I'll have it build a server on my NAS. I'll set up a working dev pipeline. I'll start small, but I'll tell it my end goal so it knows what we're working towards. 

I never did 3js I'll either do 2d or unreal engine.
